conceptPrimer.heading: Surface Tension as Force AND Energy
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $S = \frac{F}{\ell}$ ($\text{N/m}$) equals isothermal surface energy per unit area $\frac{W}{\Delta A}$ ($\text{J/m}^2$), dimension $[MT^{-2}]$. A liquid DROP in air has ONE surface; a SOAP FILM/BUBBLE has TWO. Micro-check: raising a soap film's area by $0.02\,\text{m}^2$ (both surfaces) with $S = 0.03$: $W = 2\times0.03\times0.02 = 1.2\,\text{mJ}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Coalescence: Droplets Merge, Heat Comes Out
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $n$ droplets of radius $r$ merge into one of radius $R = n^{1/3}r$ (volume conservation). Total surface area DROPS ($n\times4\pi r^2 \to 4\pi n^{2/3}r^2$), so surface energy decreases and energy is RELEASED (warming). Micro-check: $n = 8$: $R = 2r$, area ratio $= \frac{8}{4} = 2$ — halves.

conceptPrimer.heading: Young–Laplace Excess Pressure
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Concave side sits at higher pressure. Liquid drop in air or air bubble in water (ONE interface): $\Delta P = \frac{2S}{R}$. Soap bubble in air (TWO interfaces): $\Delta P = \frac{4S}{R}$. Micro-check: $S = 0.025$, $R = 0.05$: bubble $\Delta P = 2\,\text{Pa}$, drop $\Delta P = 1\,\text{Pa}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Small Bubble Beats Big Bubble
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Since $\Delta P \propto 1/R$, the smaller bubble has HIGHER internal pressure: connect a small and a large soap bubble by a tube and air flows from SMALL to LARGE — the small shrinks, the large grows. Micro-check: $R$ halves $\Rightarrow \Delta P$ doubles.

conceptPrimer.heading: Angle of Contact & Jurin's Capillary Rise
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Wetting liquids ($\theta < 90°$, water-on-clean-glass $\approx 0°$): concave meniscus, RISE. Non-wetting ($\theta > 90°$, mercury-glass $\approx 135°$): convex meniscus, DEPRESS. Height $h = \frac{2S\cos\theta}{r\rho g}$. Micro-check: water, $S = 0.07$, $r = 0.5\,\text{mm}$, $\rho = 1000$: $h = \frac{0.14}{0.0005\times10^4} = 0.028\,\text{m} = 2.8\,\text{cm}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Tube of Insufficient Length: Never a Fountain
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: If the tube is shorter than $h$, water does NOT overflow: the meniscus FLATTENS — its radius of curvature grows so that $h'R_{\text{meniscus}} = \text{const}$ (product of height and curvature radius is fixed). Micro-check: halve the protruding length $\Rightarrow$ meniscus radius doubles.

memoryHooks: Air bubble in water: ONE interface — trap.
$\Delta P \propto 1/R$: small bubble wins, air flows small $\to$ large.
Insufficient length: meniscus flattens, never a fountain.
commonMistakes: Using $\frac{4S}{R}$ for a drop or an in-liquid air bubble.
Reversing the small/large bubble flow direction.
Quoting $\frac{2S}{R}$ for a soap bubble in air (it is $\frac{4S}{R}$).
Expecting overflow from a short capillary tube.
Forgetting BOTH surfaces of a soap film in work/energy counts.
Sign error in $\cos\theta$ for non-wetting liquids.
examChecklist: Count interfaces (1 vs 2) before quoting excess pressure.
Count free interfaces (1 vs 2) before any pressure or work question.
Apply $R = n^{1/3}r$ and the energy-release argument.
Predict small-to-large air flow with $\Delta P = 4S/R$.
Energy per new area: $S\Delta A$ (double for films).
